songInfo.title: No Excuses
songInfo.tuning: Half-Step Down (Eb Ab Db Gb Bb Eb)

scalesUsed.notes: A - B - C# - D - E - F# - G - A
scalesUsed.application: Forms the open-drone acoustic verse and chorus harmony with Badd4, Asus2, G6, and Dadd9 voicings

scalesUsed.notes: F# - A - B - C# - E - F#
scalesUsed.application: Drives Jerry Cantrell's melodic, country-blues-inflected electric guitar solo

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Hypnotic open-string acoustic drone combining bright A major / Badd4 chime with brooding grunge minor shadows
keyAndScale.keySignature: 3 sharps (F#, C#, G# in fretboard shapes; sounds a half-step lower in Ab major)
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: F# minor is the relative minor of A major

mainProgression.progression: I - II - I (Verse) | I - bVII - IV - I (Chorus)
mainProgression.progressionDescription: Built entirely around open B and high E drone strings: the verse slides a movable shape between Asus2 (2nd fret) and Badd4 (4th fret) with a chromatic C-natural passing stab, while the chorus opens into lush G6 and Dadd9 chords.
mainProgression.description: Built entirely around open B and high E drone strings: the verse slides a movable shape between Asus2 (2nd fret) and Badd4 (4th fret) with a chromatic C-natural passing stab, while the chorus opens into lush G6 and Dadd9 chords.

sectionProgressions.description: Syncopated acoustic strumming sliding between fret 2 (Asus2) and fret 4 (Badd4) while strings 1 and 2 ring open

sectionProgressions.section: Chorus ('Everyday it's something, hits me all so cold')
sectionProgressions.description: Soaring Mixolydian chorus progression supporting Layne Staley and Jerry Cantrell's stacked vocal harmonies
Jerry Cantrell's lyrical electric lead solo blending F# minor / A major pentatonic bends and double-stops
A major / F# minor pentatonic country-grunge solo run

harmonicFunction: Asus2 (I) - Shimmering open-string tonic without a third, creating ambiguous grunge warmth
Badd4 (II) - Lydian-flavored major second chord with open B and E strings creating a lush 11th suspension
G6 (bVII) - Mixolydian flat-seventh chord giving the chorus its bittersweet downward pull
Dadd9 (IV) - Subdominant chord that resolves smoothly back to the A tonic

techniques.name: Open-String Drone Chord Sliding & Syncopated Strumming
techniques.description: Sliding power-chord-style shapes along the A, D, and G strings while keeping the fingers arched so the open B and high E strings ring continuously as a harmonic pedal point

sequence: Start with a quick chromatic slide from C (X-3-5-5-0-0) down to Badd4 (X-2-4-4-0-0)
Slide between Asus2 (X-0-2-2-0-0) and Badd4 (X-2-4-4-0-0) using crisp 16th-note strumming
Keep your ring and pinky fingers arched steeply so they never choke the open B and high E strings
Open up into wide strums across A, G6, and Dadd9 during the chorus
tips: Use only the tip of your ring and pinky fingers on the D and G strings so the B string stays completely unobstructed
Listen closely to Sean Kinney's bongos and snare rim-clicks in the intro to lock in the syncopated 16th-note accents
For the solo, target the major 3rd (C#) on the A chord and the natural 4th/flat-7th on the G and D chords
details.progression: Asus2 - Badd4 | A - G6 - Dadd9 - A

sections.name: Intro & Verse Open-Drone Riff
sections.technique: Open-String Drone Chord Sliding & Syncopated Strumming
sections.description: Jerry Cantrell's signature acoustic riff sliding between Asus2 and Badd4 with a C-to-B chromatic pickup.
notes: Let the open B and high E strings ring across every chord change
Hit the quick 3rd-to-2nd fret slide on the A string cleanly
Keep your right wrist loose for the sixteenth-note strumming groove

sections.name: Chorus ('Find me sitting by myself')
sections.description: Expansive chorus progression (A - G6 - Dadd9 - A) with rich vocal harmony support.
notes: Emphasize the bass root movement from A down to G and D
Keep the high E string open on G6 and Dadd9 for continuous shimmer

sections.name: Cantrell Melodic Electric Solo
sections.technique: A Major / F# Minor Pentatonic Lead
sections.description: Tasteful, vocal-like electric guitar solo combining double-stops, slides, and expressive bends.
notes: Slide smoothly into the 6th fret G string (C#) and 5th fret B string (E) double-stop
Bend the 7th fret G string up a whole step and release cleanly
Resolve the phrase on the root A note

guitar.recommended: Guild D-55 Acoustic Dreadnought & G&L Rampage Electric (for solo)
guitar.pickup: Acoustic dreadnought mic'd in stereo; Bridge humbucker on electric for the solo

amp.recommended: Bogner Fish Preamp into MosValve Power Amp (for electric overdubs & solo)

settings.gain: 6 (creamy mid-gain lead sustain for the solo)

effects.distortion: Smooth tube preamp overdrive on the electric guitar solo
effects.delay: Subtle stereo delay on the solo
effects.other: 0.73mm Dunlop Tortex pick for crisp acoustic strumming

beginner.title: Open Drone Shapes & Chorus Chords
steps: Fret Asus2 (X-0-2-2-0-0) and Badd4 (X-2-4-4-0-0) while checking that the top two strings ring clearly
Practice sliding smoothly between the 2nd and 4th frets without losing finger arch
Strum the chorus progression (A - G6 - Dadd9 - A) in steady quarter notes

intermediate.title: Syncopated Verse Groove & Chromatic Pickup
steps: Add the quick C-to-B (3rd to 2nd fret) chromatic slide at the start of the verse riff
Lock in the syncopated 16th-note strumming pattern at 116 BPM
Play through the full acoustic arrangement from intro to outro

advanced.title: Cantrell's Electric Solo & Double-Stops
steps: Learn Jerry Cantrell's electric guitar solo note-for-note including the 6th-interval double-stops
Nail the unison bends and pre-bends in the second half of the solo
Sing the high or low harmony vocal line while playing the syncopated acoustic riff

commonMistakes: Flattening the ring or pinky finger and accidentally muting the open B string on Badd4
Strumming the low E string during the Asus2 and Badd4 verse chords
Playing the verse rhythm too stiffly instead of letting the wrist swing in sixteenth notes
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Arched-finger check on Badd4 (plucking strings 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 individually)
5 minutes: Chromatic C → Badd4 → Asus2 slide drill at 95 BPM → 116 BPM
5 minutes: Chorus A → G6 → Dadd9 transitions
5 minutes: Electric solo double-stop and bending practice
focusAreas: Unobstructed open B and high E drone strings
Clean A-string muting of the low E string with the tip of the index finger
Melodic double-stop intonation in the solo
metronomeWork: Start at 90 BPM to master the syncopated verse strumming accents
Increase to 116 BPM while keeping the sixteenth-note ghost strums light
Practice the solo entrance timing right out of the second chorus
